Michael (2026) is the long-awaited Michael Jackson biopic directed by Antoine Fuqua, written by John Logan, and produced by Graham King (the producer behind Bohemian Rhapsody). The film stars Jackson's real-life nephew, Jaafar Jackson, in his film debut as the King of Pop, alongside Colman Domingo and Nia Long as his parents Joe and Katherine Jackson, Miles Teller as attorney John Branca, Larenz Tate as Motown founder Berry Gordy, Laura Harrier as music executive Suzanne de Passe, Kat Graham as Diana Ross, and Kendrick Sampson as Quincy Jones.

Made on a roughly $155 million budget and distributed by Lionsgate domestically (with Universal handling international release), the movie traces Jackson's life from childhood to his death, covering both his public triumphs and private struggles, and runs about 2 hours 10 minutes with a PG-13 rating for thematic material, language, and smoking.

Originally slated for an October 2025 release, it was delayed to April 24, 2026 due to reshoots and a lengthy editing process, but generated massive anticipation along the way, its November 2025 trailer drew 116.2 million views in 24 hours, a record for a music biopic or concert film. Since its release, reception has been mixed, with some critics calling it a fairly conventional, somewhat sanitized biopic that softens Jackson's more controversial moments, though Jaafar Jackson's performance has been widely praised; there's also been talk of a possible sequel covering the latter half of Jackson's life.

A penalty shootout between Corinthians and São Paulo produced one of those bizarre football moments that looks almost too ridiculous to be real. As the player in black and white stripes approaches the spot, the goalkeeper prepares for a conventional penalty, expecting the usual walk back, run-up and strike. Instead, the execution catches everyone off guard, turning a routine kick into a moment that football fans would keep debating long after the match. The joke in the post is that the penalty was so outrageous it supposedly "traumatized FIFA" into changing the rules forever. But that is the exaggeration that makes the meme work: Brazilian football has a long history of unconventional penalty techniques, and whenever someone finds a way to catch a goalkeeper completely unprepared, fans immediately start joking about whether the laws of the game will need rewriting. Penalty rules have indeed evolved over the years, including clarifications about feinting during the run-up, goalkeeper positioning and double touches. Under the current laws, a kicker who illegally feints after completing the run-up can be penalized, while the goalkeeper must meet specific positioning requirements when the ball is struck. However, there is no clear evidence that this specific Corinthians-São Paulo kick caused FIFA or IFAB to introduce a permanent rule change. The caption is best understood as football humour rather than a literal account of the laws changing because of one penalty.

Rúben Amorim arrived at AC Milan in June 2026 after his spell at Manchester United, taking over from Massimiliano Allegri and beginning a completely new chapter in Serie A. From the start, Milan were expected to bring the Portuguese coach's trademark intensity, pressing and possession-based football to San Siro. The clearest example came in the 3-0 win over Lecce. Rather than forcing the team into a rigid structure, Amorim gave his players more freedom, changed the way Milan built from the back and allowed different players to move into positions that suited their strengths. The result was a much more fluid attacking performance, with Christian Pulisic opening the scoring before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira completed the win. For Amorim, it was also about learning from his Manchester United experience. He admitted afterward that he could not make the same tactical mistake again when his players did not perfectly fit a particular structure. Against Lecce, Milan looked more flexible, aggressive and mobile - exactly the kind of football Amorim was brought in to build.

Zlatan Ibrahimović delivered his first hat-trick for Manchester United on February 16, 2017, helping José Mourinho’s side secure a 3–0 victory over Saint-Étienne in the first leg of their Europa League round-of-32 tie at Old Trafford. It was a performance that perfectly captured Zlatan’s ability to decide games, even without producing three spectacular finishes. His opener arrived in the 15th minute when a free-kick struck the defensive wall, deflected off Vincent Pajot and slowly rolled past goalkeeper Stéphane Ruffier. It certainly wasn’t the kind of goal that would win a beauty contest, but United had the lead, and Zlatan was already on his way to another memorable night against a familiar opponent. The second goal came in the 75th minute after Marcus Rashford created the opportunity with excellent work down the left, allowing Ibrahimović to finish from close range. Then, with only minutes remaining, Zlatan won a penalty after going down under a challenge from Kevin Théophile-Catherine and calmly converted it in the 88th minute to complete his treble. The funny part is that all three goals were so straightforward that the hat-trick almost feels out of character for a striker famous for spectacular finishes and moments of individual brilliance. A deflected free-kick, a tap-in and a penalty—nothing particularly outrageous, yet all three counted exactly the same on the scoreboard. Even contemporary match coverage described the treble as one of his scruffier hat-tricks. But that was Zlatan: he didn’t need every goal to be beautiful, because his job was to make sure the ball ended up in the net. United eventually progressed with a 4–0 aggregate victory, and this remained Ibrahimović’s only hat-trick in a Manchester United shirt. Sometimes the ugliest hat-tricks are just as effective as the most spectacular ones—and Zlatan made sure this one counted.

Prayer isn't only about asking God for the things we want. It's also an opportunity to reflect, express gratitude, seek wisdom, and bring our deepest concerns before Him. Sometimes we pray for a solution. Other times, we pray for patience, courage, or the ability to face a difficult situation with grace.

A consistent prayer life can help us become more intentional about our choices and more aware of the people and blessings we sometimes overlook. It encourages us to pause in the middle of a busy world and remember that our struggles do not have to define our entire story.

You don't need perfect words to pray. You can begin with an honest heart, sharing your concerns and asking for guidance as you move forward.

When life feels uncertain, make time for prayer. When you experience blessings, remember gratitude. And when someone else is struggling, consider offering a prayer and practical support.

Many people spend years searching for their purpose. We wonder what we're meant to do, where our talents belong, and how we can make our lives meaningful. These questions become especially important when our current path leaves us feeling uncertain or unfulfilled.

Faith invites us to consider a deeper perspective. Instead of focusing exclusively on personal achievements, we can ask how our gifts, experiences, and opportunities might be used to serve others and honor God.

Purpose doesn't always appear as one dramatic moment or a perfectly clear plan. Sometimes it develops through ordinary decisions: showing compassion, helping someone in need, becoming more patient, supporting a family member, or using our abilities to make a positive difference.
